title: Research
text: My research interests lie at the intersection of epidemiology, mental health, and quantitative methods. I am particularly interested in understanding how psychological, social, and biological factors shape mental health across the life course.

title: Research
text:
Main research areas

Psychiatric epidemiology
Population-level research on the development, course, and prevention of mental disorders, particularly bipolar-spectrum symptoms and early indicators of psychiatric risk.


Perinatal mental health
Maternal mental health during pregnancy and after birth, including risk factors, consequences for parents and children, and opportunities for prevention.


Child and adolescent health
Longitudinal research on mental health and development during childhood and adolescence, including the role of family, social, and physical-health factors.


Health inequalities
How socioeconomic conditions and unequal access to resources influence mental and physical health across populations.

title: Research
text:
Selected projects

Mania in youth
A longitudinal study using data from more than 10,000 participants in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study. Latent trajectory modelling was used to identify distinct patterns of manic symptoms and investigate their psychological, familial, and physical-health correlates.


ManyBabies
Contributions to international collaborative projects examining infant habituation, neonatal imitation, and digital-media exposure in early childhood.


International collaborative research
Participation in large-scale multi-country projects focused on mental health, risk-taking, and reproducible team science.

title: About me
text:
I am a clinical psychologist and quantitative health researcher currently completing a master’s degree in epidemiology at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz.
My academic work combines substantive knowledge of mental health with statistical and epidemiological methods. I am particularly interested in psychiatric and perinatal epidemiology, child and adolescent mental health, register-based research, and health inequalities.

title: About me
text:
Background
I hold degrees in psychology and clinical psychology and psychotherapy from the University of Göttingen. My previous research has included longitudinal mental health research, international multi-site collaborations, developmental psychology, and clinical neuroscience.

title: About me
text:
Methods
My methodological experience includes:

Data preparation and reproducible analysis in R
Regression and mixed-effects models
Longitudinal analysis
Latent trajectory modelling
Causal inference
Machine learning and prediction
Collaborative and multi-analyst research

title: About me
text:
Looking ahead
My long-term goal is to conduct a PhD in psychiatric or perinatal epidemiology using large-scale cohort or register data. I am always interested in meeting researchers working in these areas and contributing to collaborative projects.

title: Jasmin Dönicke
text:
I am a clinical psychologist and epidemiology master’s student with experience in health data analysis, medical statistics, and international collaborative research.
My work focuses particularly on psychiatric and perinatal epidemiology, child and adolescent mental health, health inequalities, and the use of longitudinal and causal methods to study population health.
